source: Hawkes Studio (generic conventions for every customer's Studio)
about: How a Hawkes Studio works, true for every studio: no one's decisions, preferences or story. The owner's own come from their words in Talk.

entries.title: Playtest bots play through real input
entries.body: A scenario presses the keys, clicks and touches a player would, into the game's own input layer. No teleporting or state edits; a named setup shortcut is fine.

entries.title: Every game keeps a working smoke scenario
entries.body: The smoke scenario loads the game, plays a little and checks nothing errors. Keep it passing when changing the game.

entries.title: Agent changes go to beta first
entries.body: An agent works on its own branch and opens a pull request into the game's beta branch. Nothing reaches the live game until the owner goes live.

entries.title: Make acceptance criteria observable
entries.body: Each criterion is something a player sees or can do, shown by a scenario event, a metric or a scene, so a playtest review can judge it.

entries.title: Generated assets go through Hawkes Gen
entries.body: Images, video, voice, sound, music and 3D are made with Hawkes Gen's tools, never with keys of an agent's own. Price GPU work first.

entries.title: Never hand-edit generated output
entries.body: Build output, engine-generated folders and lock files are made by their tools: change the source and rebuild.

entries.title: Small, focused changes
entries.body: One task, one pull request: the smallest correct change, no unrelated cleanups, no new dependencies unless the task needs one.
